paper_metadata.title: Tensile behavior at various temperatures of the Mg-Gd-Y-Zn-Zr alloys with different initial morphologies of LPSO phases prior to extrusion

evidence.quote: The tensile behavior at ( 100)-300 ◦ C of the extruded and peak-aged Mg-5Gd-3Y-xZn-0.5Zr (x = 1 and 2 wt%, designated as VWZ531K and VWZ532K) alloys was investigated in the aspects of microstructural evolution, deformation modes, mechanical properties, etc.

The tensile behavior at various temperatures of the extruded or peak-aged Mg-5Gd-3Y-(1, 2)Zn-0.5Zr (VWZ531K, VWZ532K) alloys was investigated in the aspects of microstructural evolution, deformation modes, mechanical properties, etc.

After homogenization at 510 ◦ C for 24 h, cylindrical billets with a diameter of Φ 50 mm were machined from the center of the ingots.

After being held at 400 ◦ C for 1 h, the cylindrical billets were extruded in an extrusion container of Φ 52 mm into bars of Φ 10 mm, at the ram speed of 1 mm/s and with the extrusion ratio of ~27, followed by air cooling.
Aging treatment after extrusion was conducted at 200 ◦ C in an air furnace.

numerous nano-scale β′ precipitates endow the VWZ531K alloy with the much higher TYS compared with the VWZ532K at almost all testing temperatures except for 300 °C, since β′ precipitates were reported to effectively inhibit the movement of basal dislocations and therefore provide the strong strengthening effect [40].

At the as-extruded state, the VWZ531K alloy contains a much higher solid solution strengthening effect due to the less volume fraction of block interdendritic LPSO phases which consume solute atoms and result in the less RE and Zn content in the α-Mg matrix (see Table 2).
